G. V . Mavalankar became the first Speaker of the First Lok Sabha (लोकसभा) of independent India on 15 May 1952 and remained in office until his death on 27 February 1956. He is also known as the “Father of the Lok Sabha” for laying the foundations of parliamentary procedure, rules, and traditions. This title was conferred on him by J.L. Nehru.

Vigneshwar Missir and Acharya J.B. Kripalani, with 21 Parliament (संसद) members of the opposition, moved a No- Confidence Motion against First Lok Sabha Speaker G.V. Mavalankar on 15 December, 1954. This motion was refused by the Lok Sabha on 18 December, 1954.
The first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha (लोकसभा) was Meira Kumar. She was chosen unopposed as Speaker and served from June 2009 to June 2014.

Meira Kumar was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Meira Kumar was an Indian diplomat, politician, and government official who served as speaker of the 15 th Lok Sabha (Lower Chamber of the Indian Parliament (संसद)) from 2009 to 2014, the first woman to hold that position.

Balayogi; the Speaker of the 14th Lok Sabha was Somnath Chatterjee; and the Speaker of the 17th Lok Sabha was Om Birla. At present, the Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha is also Om Birla (second term). According to Article 95 of the Indian Constitution, when the office of Speaker is vacant, its duties shall be performed by the Deputy Speaker, who can vote in the event of an equality (समता) of votes, while others are not the rights of the Speaker.
On 23 May 1996, P.A. Sangma became the first tribal speaker of the 11th Lok Sabha (लोकसभा).

The Lok Sabha Secretariat works under the direction and control of the Speaker of the House. The Secretariat has supreme authority over its employees, premises, and assets of the Parliament (संसद) and exercises this authority through the Secretary (as provided by Article 98 and rules 124 and 124-A).
